description: Two invented earlier sessions in the email digital twin (Northwind Mail), as confirmed Work Maps. Loaded only when AGENT_SEED_MAPS=1 and no confirmed map exists; in memory only, never written to the maps file. Synthetic data: every name, address and quote is made up. No screen moments: nothing here was recorded.

processes.title: Invoice email: payment terms
processes.summary: Send a customer their invoice by email with the payment terms their agreement allows.

steps.action: Opened the draft "Invoice INV-2188" to billing@harbor-print.example in Northwind Mail; the last line of the message said "Payment terms: Net 14."

steps.goal: Check which customer the invoice is for
steps.action: Read the recipient and the subject, then looked the customer up in the list of signed agreements

steps.goal: Set the payment terms the customer is entitled to
steps.action: Changed "Net 14" to "Net 30" in the last line of the message

decision.summary: Net 30 instead of the standard Net 14 for a customer with a signed agreement
decision.reason: The customer has a signed agreement for Net 30
decision.quote: Harbor Print has a signed agreement, so it gets Net 30. The standard is Net 14.

steps.action: Pressed Send with the invoice PDF attached and the agreed terms in the last line

guardrails.condition: Payment terms longer than the standard Net 14 on an invoice email
guardrails.requiredAction: Net 30 only for a customer with a signed agreement; anything longer than Net 30 needs the finance lead
guardrails.reason: Only customers with a signed agreement are entitled to longer terms
guardrails.quote: If they have a signed agreement it is Net 30. Anything longer, I ask the finance lead first.
exceptions: A customer without a signed agreement keeps the standard Net 14

map.teachBack: Here is what I understood. Invoice emails use the standard Net 14. A customer with a signed agreement gets Net 30, and anything longer needs the finance lead. Is that right?

processes.title: Delivery update email
processes.summary: Send a customer the delivery address and time of their order, in the form they asked for.

steps.action: Opened the draft "Delivery update — ORD-2049" to customer_07 in Northwind Mail with delivery-summary.png attached and an empty message
Looked at the attached image and the order: the delivery address and the delivery time

steps.goal: Put the delivery details in the message text
steps.action: Typed the delivery address and the delivery time into the message, and kept the image attached

decision.summary: Details as text for customer_07, not only in the image
decision.reason: customer_07 asked to get the delivery details as text
decision.quote: customer_07 asked to get the address and the time as text, so I write them in the email.

steps.action: Pressed Send with the details in the text and the image still attached

guardrails.condition: A delivery update email to customer_07 has no delivery address and time in its text
guardrails.requiredAction: Add the delivery address and time as text before sending
guardrails.reason: customer_07 asked to get them as text
guardrails.quote: customer_07 asked to get the address and the time as text.
exceptions: An image is fine when the details are also in the text

map.teachBack: Here is what I understood. A delivery update to customer_07 needs the delivery address and time written in the email, because customer_07 asked for text. An image is fine as an extra when the details are also in the text. Is that right?
